note: Upstream runtime archives per target. A sha256 stays null until it is verified: the release operator downloads each archive, verifies it against the vendor's own published integrity data, and pins the lowercase SHA-256 here. scripts/release/stage-runtime.ts refuses a null pin with RUNTIME_SOURCE_UNPINNED and a null url with RUNTIME_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. URLs were checked to resolve on 2026-10-14; layouts and license paths were read from the archive listings. Entries with official=false come from a third-party redistributor because the upstream project ships no relocatable build for that target; their provenance needs separate review.

win32-arm64.note: EnterpriseDB publishes no windows-arm64 zip binaries at the x64 URL pattern (the equivalent URL is refused). Identify a genuine arm64 build before releasing this target.

darwin-x64.note: Universal Mach-O (x86_64 and arm64). lib/ holds dylib symlinks that staging materialises as regular files.
python.org ships only a non-relocatable macOS installer package, so this third-party relocatable build is used.

darwin-arm64.note: Universal Mach-O (x86_64 and arm64). lib/ holds dylib symlinks that staging materialises as regular files.

readers.note: Bundled PDF readers per target, staged into an already-staged runtime by `stage-runtime.ts --readers` (or `--readers-only`). Python packages come from the hash-pinned requirement file (pip --require-hashes, one wheel per package, every hash equal to PyPI's JSON API digest). tesseract comes from conda-forge packages pinned by their repodata sha256; only the files in `include` (bin/tesseract and its shared-library closure, glibc excluded) are copied, symlinks materialised, plus every package's info/licenses. eng.traineddata is pinned separately. A target whose `include` is null has never been staged and refuses.
